task: Making classic hummus with lemon and garlic
query: How do I make classic hummus with lemon and garlic?

goal.title: Make hummus in a food processor
goal.description: Rinse canned chickpeas, combine them with tahini, oil, trimmed garlic and squeezed lemon in a processor, then blend in several passes with additional tahini, oil and white seasoning between passes.
goal.final_state: A beige chickpea paste remains around the blade in the open processor jug. It has been stirred and sampled with a spoon; mouth contact and serving are not visible.

procedure.description: Pull open the chickpea can, carry it to the sink and retrieve a mesh strainer. Pour and shake the chickpeas into the strainer, set the can aside and rinse the chickpeas under running water while shaking them. Move the processor jug beside the sink, lift it and tip the drained chickpeas inside. Put the strainer in the sink and return the filled jug to the counter.

Open the tahini jar and stir its contents with a spoon, but then put the jar down and rinse and rub the spoon under the tap. Shut off the water, lift the jar again and scrape a spoonful of tahini onto the chickpeas. Put the jar aside, change the spoon to the left hand, uncap the oil bottle and fill the spoon with oil. Tip the oil into the processor, return the bottle, wipe the spoon and put it in the small bowl in the sink. Briefly withdraw and inspect the hands.

Adjust the processor blade by its central shaft, briefly move between garlic on the board and the jug, then take a knife. Hold and trim garlic cloves on the board, repeatedly repositioning them and scraping their skins. Put the knife down to pull away papery skin with the fingertips, pick it up for additional trimming, then peel again. Drop the peeled clove into the jug, retrieve another piece, cut it into smaller pieces and drop those into the jug too.

Put the knife down and lift a previously cut lemon half. Separate the lemon pieces, hold the half above the processor and repeatedly squeeze and work its pulp with the fingertips. Put the squeezed half on the board, pick up and fit the processor lid, seat the motor on it, then extend and untangle the power cord and plug it into the wall outlet.

Reposition the processor and press its motor button to blend the ingredients. Remove and set down the motor and lid, retrieve a spoon from the drawer and stir and lift a sample of the coarse chickpea mixture. Exchange spoons at the drawer, retrieve the tahini jar and scrape another spoonful into the processor. Put the spoon in the sink, pour additional oil directly from its bottle, return the jar and fit the lid and motor again.

Hold the processor button for a longer blend, producing a finer beige paste. Remove and set down the motor and lid, retrieve the spoon, scrape the walls and stir and lift another sample. Mouth contact is out of view. Retrieve the small shaker, shake white seasoning into the jug and return the shaker to the counter.

Replace the lid and motor, run a final short blend, remove and set down the motor and uncover the jug. Retrieve the spoon, stir and scrape the paste and lift another sample before lowering the spoon near the sink. Pick up the processor lid again at the very end. The paste remains in the processor jug; transfer to a serving bowl is not shown.
